About Customer Return Analytics and Insights Report

Retail Business Services - Brand Experience (BX) team, offers Customer Return Analytics and Insights (CRAI) to assist global brands on Amazon in improving and promoting product rating above 4 stars. This tool helps selling partners improve their products by analyzing customer feedback, sentiment, and performance compared to top competitors. Using Generative AI technology, the CRAI report identifies key factors from 'customer returns and negative reviews' to provide actionable recommendations for enhancing products.

The report consists of 2 main sheets:

  • Brand Report Section: This section provides a comprehensive overview of defects and performance metrics at brand level, Marketplace level, Product category and GL level.
  • All ASIN Summary Section: This section provides a comprehensive overview of defects and performance metrics at CASIN level, brand level, marketplace level, product category, and GL level.
Brand Report Section:
  1. This section provides a comprehensive overview of defects and performance metrics at various levels, including Brand, Product Category, GL, and Marketplace.

  2. The Brand Performance Metrics provides valuable insights into T3M Return Rate, T3M Returned units, T3M shipped units, display rating, T3M Critical review rate, and conversion, enabling us to assess the reception of the listings. Further, examining Brand Performance Trends helps determine whether these are isolated occurrences or consistent patterns.

  3. Brand Defect Overview reveals the top defects within the selected filters. This section highlights customer complaints, defect occurrences over the past three months, and defect type (catalog or non-catalog). Identifying these issues at the Brand, category, GL, or Marketplace level directs our focus to the All ASIN Summary sheet for a deeper analysis.

All ASIN Summary Section:
  1. After identifying issues at the Brand, Marketplace, Product Category, or GL level, we can delve deeper to pinpoint ASINs in these categories and obtain C-ASIN Level Insights. Select the desired C-ASIN to access Product Performance Trend . Return rate, Display rating, % Critical Review, and Conversion graphical representation provides more insights on metrics trend.

  2. Product performance table provides ASIN, Brand, T3M Return rate, Top issues identified, Fixed recommendation, Key phrase and defect images.

  3. T12 M Defect Trend graph represents the selected ASIN defect trend for the review.

  4. Detailed Report section provides the table which contains information about defects reported by customers for all ASINs based on the criteria chosen. The criteria are

    1. Top 10 ASINs with highest return Rate
    2. Bottom 10 ASINs based on Product Performance score
    3. Top 10 ASINs with Lowest Star Rating
Note:
  • Both sheets have interactive filters at Brand, Marketplace, General Ledger, Product Category and ASIN level that selling partners can apply and view summaries. Select One Brand, Marketplace, Product Category and General ledger in the Brand Report Section and Select One Brand, Marketplace, Product Category and General ledger and C-ASIN in ASIN Report Section as multiselection is disabled.

Here are some definitions to help you understand the report better:

  1. Critical Review: TA review with a star rating below 3 and with a negative polarity.
  2. # Mentions: Absolute number of times the topic under consideration appeared in the customer reviews in trailing six months (T6M).
  3. Conversion: It is the Percentage of shipped units out of the total visits on the Product Detailed Page.
  4. ASIN: Amazon Standard Identification Number. It is used to uniquely identify all products in the retail catalog.
  5. Child ASIN: The Child ASIN refers to the specific variation of the product (e.g., Levi’s 501 Jeans in size large and color black).
  6. Marketplace: A Marketplace is a place, physical or otherwise, where merchants offer goods for sale, and customers accept offers, place orders and make purchases.
  7. MCID: Merchant Customer ID. It is a unique ID that identifies selling partners on Amazon.
  8. T3M: Trailing 3 Months.
  9. T12M: Trailing 12 months.
  10. Defect: A defect is a categorized customer complaint derived from Reviews & Returns.
  11. General Ledger (GL):It is a distinct product grouping that differentiates items like books from watches or video games. It is a broader classification than Product Category.
  12. Fix Recommendation: It will enable you with recommendations on
    1. What issues to act
    2. How to act, along with CX insights that you can act upon
  13. Conversion Rate: It is a key performance metric used to measure the effectiveness of the product. It refers to the percentage of number of conversions(shipped units) to the total number of visits to the product page.
  14. Post Purchase Analytics: (PPA) is a feature that provides customer segment-level insights derived from reviews, Customer Questions & Answers (CQA), and returns data.
  15. Size & Fit: This feature provides visibility into Size & Fit defects in order to fix those defects in the catalog.
  16. Review Summarization: It is a feature that provides key defects aggregated at a level selected across filters leveraging-
    1. Key phrases from return comments
    2. Customer sentiment at ASIN defect level
  17. Estimated Lost Opportunity: It is a data-driven tool that quantifies the potential revenue loss (OPS impact) from product defects by analyzing customer feedback data and returns.
  18. At Risk of HRRA: It represents whether the ASIN is at risk of being categorized as a high return rate ASIN.
  19. High Return Rate ASINs: It represents whether the ASIN is categorized as a high return rate ASIN.
  20. Conceded Units: Total conceded units (returned, replaced, refunded or other compensations) for the Parent ASIN.
  21. Shipped Units: Total shipped units of all Child ASINs (CASIN) within a Parent ASIN (PASIN).
  22. Concession Rate: The percentage of conceded units relative to shipped units. Formula: (Conceded Units / Shipped Units) x 100.

How to use the catalog improvement opportunity insights ?
This table summarizes set of recommendations that enables Brands to understand the customer anecdotes from returns/CQA at scale & get upfront sense of ROI to implement the catalog changes. It has the following key data points for a given ASIN:
Content Missing in the Detail page: Topic to add in detail page based on scalable analysis of Customer anecdotes coming from FAQ sections of detail page.
No. of times Customers asked for this detail (at category level): #CQA asked at category level in that topic to give a sense of problem scale at the category level.
Ideal Location to add this content: Suggested section to add, to recommend SP the ideal location in DP to add the content for maximum customer & business impact.
% top ASINs in this category with this content in their detail page: A benchmark of how many top selling ASINs in this category have this contents in their detail pages
Expected impact on return rate (in %): Estimated return impact thats calculated through our statistical model.
For Eg. ASIN B00XXXXXXX belongs to PT_RUG.
Signal 1: In this PT, customers frequently ask questions related to the topic “fabric/material type”.
Signal 2: In this PT, customers frequently return the products related to the defects of “fabric/material type”.
Hence in this table we will recommend the brand to add “fabric/material type” contents in the detail page of ASIN B00XXXXXXX, to reduce returns by xx%.
Note: These insights are generated by AI/ML models and is expected to give a directional guidance to brands for improving catalog. We recommend the brands owners to verify the applicability of recommended topic to the target ASINs before making catalog changes.

Catalogue Recommendation — Catalogue Completeness NEW
How to use the catalogue completeness insights?
Each row flags a catalog defect on one of your ASINs and quantifies why it is worth fixing. Two metrics help you prioritize:

Glance Views (T3M): how many shoppers landed on this ASIN’s detail page in the last 3 months. More glance views = more shoppers exposed to the defect, so the upside of fixing it is larger.
% of top 10% selling ASINs in this category with this attribute complete: a benchmark of how many of the best-selling ASINs in this Product Type already have the attribute right — what the products outselling you are already doing.

There are two recommendation types: Purchase corrects a title that does not match the variant a customer selects; Discovery & Evaluation ask you to complete a missing attribute.
Purchase — Detail-page / cart title mismatch

The detail page shows the parent title. When a customer selects a child variant and adds it to cart, the cart shows a title whose size/colour does not match the selected variant. Correcting the title removes this surprise at purchase and the returns it drives.

Discovery & Evaluation — Attribute incompleteness

These ASINs are missing a structured attribute that customers use to find and evaluate the product. Completing it improves discoverability, sets correct expectations, and reduces returns.

Catalogue Recommendation — Product Video NEW
How to use the video recommendation insights?

This table flags ASINs missing a product video on the detail page. Video is one of the first things shoppers look for to understand assembly, fit, and how a product actually looks — and its absence drives avoidable returns and lost purchases. Two metrics help you decide where to act first:

Glance Views (T90D): how many shoppers landed on this ASIN’s detail page in the last 90 days. More glance views = more shoppers exposed to the missing-video gap, so the upside of adding a video is larger.
% of top 10% selling ASINs in this category with a product video: a benchmark of how many of the best-selling ASINs in this Product Type already carry a video — what the products outselling you are already doing.

The Insight column ties these signals together; Videos to Upload gives the specific content guidance and next steps.

Historically, Adding a video is associated with an average 23% sales lift.

How to upload your video
  1. Log in to Seller Central
  2. Select Products
  3. Click the Manage products button
  4. Click Manage videos
  5. Upload your video and tag the relevant ASIN so it appears on the detail page

New ASINs performance predictor
New ASIN Performance Predictor analyzes your recently launched products (less than 3 months old) by leveraging data from similar, established ASINs in your category. By studying patterns from mature products, we provide early insights into potential performance challenges and proactive recommendations. This enables you to address common issues before they impact your new product's performance, helping you optimize your launch strategy.

Metric Definition
  • Product Type: A named location within a product category used for navigation, classification, and website content organization.
  • Units Sold – CPF: The average number of units sold within a specified range at a particular product type, specifically referring to CPF units (presumably referring to certain product types or categories).
  • Growth Rate % (past 180 days) – CPF: The percentage growth rate of CPF units sold within a specific product type over the past 180 days, calculated as the number of CPF units sold in the browse node divided by the total number of units sold in the browse node, multiplied by 100.
  • Units Sold – Non CPF: The average number of units sold within a specified range across all product types, including both CPF and non-CPF units.
  • Growth Rate % (past 180 days) – Non CPF: The percentage growth rate of non-CPF units sold within a specific product category over the past 180 days, calculated as the number of non-CPF units sold in the browse node divided by the total number of units sold in the browse node, multiplied by 100.
  • CPF Customer Search: The number of customer searches specifically related to CPF products at a particular product type.
  • Non-CPF Customer Search: The number of customer searches specifically related to non-CPF products at a particular product type.
  • CPF Conversion %: Conversion percentage of CPF products, indicating the percentage of CPF customer searches that result in purchases.
  • Non-CPF Conversion %: Conversion percentage of non-CPF products, indicating the percentage of non-CPF customer searches that result in purchases.
  • Keywords: Search terms or phrases that customers use to search for products.
  • All Impressions: The total number of times a product or its listing is viewed by users, irrespective of whether it leads to a purchase.
  • % Contribution - All Impressions: The percentage contribution of a specific product type or category to all impressions on the website.
  • All Purchases: The total number of purchases made across all product types or categories.
  • % Contribution - All Purchases: The percentage contribution of a specific product type or category to all purchases made on the website.
